# Test files a DEDICATED CI phase runs, and therefore the unit sweep must NOT.
#
# The unit sweep (`Phase 1` in tests.yml) discovers its work with `ls tests/test_*.py` minus this
# list. That inversion is the point: the filesystem decides what runs, and an exception has to be
# written down HERE, with a reason. The previous shape was the opposite -- fifteen filenames typed
# into the workflow -- and it silently drifted: 144 test files existed, 44 were named anywhere in
# CI, and 94 never executed at all. A new test file was inert by default and nothing said so.
# tests/test_ci_coverage.py fails when a file is in neither the sweep nor this list.
#
# A file belongs here for exactly one reason: another phase already runs it, usually because it
# needs a toolchain, a launcher or a service the cheap sweep job does not install. "It is slow"
# alone is not a reason to exclude -- it is a reason to give it its own phase and list it here.
#
# Format: one path per line, `#` comments and blank lines ignored. Read by BOTH tests.yml and
# tests/test_ci_coverage.py, so the workflow and the guard cannot disagree about what is claimed.

# --- MPI: data distribution + descriptor (pure numpy, no launcher) ------------------------------
tests/test_mpi_descriptor.py
tests/test_mpi_prompt.py
tests/test_mpi_scatter_gather_roundtrip.py
tests/test_mpi_sizing.py
tests/test_mpi_wire.py

# --- MPI: driver / stub codegen (needs mpicc.mpich to compile) ----------------------------------
tests/test_mpi_driver_codegen.py
tests/test_mpi_halo.py

# --- MPI: oversubscribed multi-rank launch (needs a working launcher) ---------------------------
tests/test_mpi_call.py
tests/test_mpi_correctness_oracle.py
tests/test_mpi_drivers_launch.py
tests/test_mpi_scoring.py
tests/test_noop_mpi_optimizer.py

# --- agent-bench: tools + optimizers + in-process judge -----------------------------------------
tests/test_agent_bench.py
tests/test_agent_service.py
tests/test_agent_tools.py
tests/test_blas_optimizer.py
tests/test_harbor_adapter.py
tests/test_noop_optimizer.py
tests/test_optimizer_plugin.py
tests/test_packaging.py
tests/test_token_usage.py

# --- codegen backends: need tvm / pluto / a full compiler matrix --------------------------------
tests/test_default_datatype_tolerance.py
tests/test_fp16.py
tests/test_frameworks.py
tests/test_native_autogen.py

# --- the long sweeps: each is its own phase, several with a backend matrix ----------------------
tests/test_e2e_numerical.py
tests/test_integration_sweep.py
tests/test_kernelbench_translation.py
# Phase 5d on frameworks-pluto: needs polycc AND dace in one process, and that is the only runner
# with both. Excluded from the unit sweep because the sweep's runner has neither Pluto nor the
# headroom -- it would skip there, and a skip that looks like a pass is what this file prevents.
tests/test_opt_reports_e2e.py

# --- containers: needs a rootless runtime on the runner -----------------------------------------
tests/test_container_launch.py

# --- QUARANTINE: not run anywhere, each needs a decision ----------------------------------------
# Nothing is quarantined today. A file added below runs NOWHERE, so it needs a one-line reason and
# an owner -- an unexplained entry here is the same silent inertness this file exists to end.

# --- port fidelity: the corpus vs what it was ported from ---------------------------------------
# Needs the whole DaCe frontend over 576 generated programs -- minutes, one subprocess each --
# which the cheap unit sweep's runner has neither the time nor the dependency for.
tests/test_dace_frontend_validity.py
# The dace-numeric runner: lowers, compiles and RUNS each generated DaCe program against numpy.
# Its own job because it is the only phase paying a C++ build PER KERNEL -- in the cheap unit
# sweep that is minutes of compiling per shard, on a runner with no per-kernel build directory.
tests/test_dace_numeric_agreement.py
# Builds OpenBLAS from source with make/gfortran, which the unit sweep's runner does not install.
tests/test_dace_openblas_link.py
# Phase 8b on the same runner: needs CPU torch plus the third_party/KernelBench submodule, neither
# of which the unit sweep's runner has -- there it would `importorskip` torch and pass without
# comparing anything. Its helper (tests/kernelbench_agreement.py) is not listed: this file names
# only test_*.py files, which is the set the sweep's `ls` and tests/test_ci_coverage.py both use.
tests/test_kernelbench_torch_agreement.py
